ops.append: Within the same paper SCAR12 organoids show the MYC-positive fraction up while the radial-glia fraction is wild-type-like and the single-cell neuron-cluster fraction is not reduced (text lines 577 and 585-586; WOREE shows reduced CTIP2/SATB2 in Fig 6B, SCAR12 is the clean case), so MYC elevation alone does not give the composition phenotype; the box medians read by eye from Fig 3K are about 18 (wild type), 68 (knockout), 45 (SCAR12) and 55 (WOREE) percent with wide scatter and overlap.
ops.reason: the existing O2 limits say the composition phenotype is a knockout feature but do not state the consequence for the driver reading

observation.statement: Neuron-promoter AAV9-WWOX added at week 10 and read at week 16 raises the CTIP2-positive and SATB2-positive fractions of nuclei in WOREE-derived organoids to wild-type level (SCAR12 is already near wild type) and lowers hyperexcitability, without differentially expressed genes or cell-cycle change in radial glia. The layer-marker deficit therefore has a reversible neuron-stage component after the radial-glia phase.
observation.genotype: WOREE-derived line, neuron-promoter WWOX add-back versus control vector
observation.comparison: add-back against control vector, and against wild type
observation.readout: CTIP2 and SATB2 fractions of nuclei (Fig 6B); radial-glia differential expression
observation.limits: Fractions of nuclei, not neuron numbers; one laboratory; no untreated WOREE group for the control vector in the shown panel; the authors state neuronal WWOX was not detected in neural organoids at this stage; an intervention response (held out for compound evaluation); overlaps the gene-addition need and must not be counted twice across needs.

ops.text: POU5F1 is as prominent as MYC in the knockout radial-glia contrast (Fig 3F: capped significance for both), which fits retained progenitor state without a MYC-specific driver.

The inverse WWOX-MYC relation in the reference datasets is a developmental time course (Fig 3H-I), and MYC is phase-coupled in the knockout only (Fig 4D): maturity and cell-cycle state can explain a MYC rise without a driver role.

MYCN dosage sets cortical size in both directions (loss: microcephaly; gain: megalencephaly; abstracts of PMIDs 15821734 and 37710961), and progressive microcephaly is part of the WOREE picture (4 of 5 in one cohort, PMID 36537114): lowering MYC-family output could shrink the progenitor pool. Not WWOX evidence.

In mouse, neuron-stage (Synapsin-Cre) deletion reproduces the null phenotype as progenitor-stage (nestin-Cre) deletion does (PMID 33914858), and neuron-stage add-back rescues without correcting radial glia: a radial-glia MYC state is not shown to be needed for the severe mouse endpoints.

ops.new: Restoring checkpoint competence or suppressing proliferation pharmacologically in a developing compartment has no safe formulation in the record (map section 2.2). A MYC-lowering lever is not assumed beneficial: MYC-family dose is two-sided in cortex, SCAR12 shows MYC elevation without the composition phenotype, and lithium (a Wnt activator) is a risk flag for this window, not a candidate.
